title: THEY RELEASED A CRIMINAL.
paragraphs: THEY RELEASED A CRIMINAL.

Not by accident.
Not by confusion.
By choice.
And the crowd knew exactly what they were doing.
Jerusalem was electric that morning.

Dust rising.
Voices shouting.
Soldiers gripping spears.
Two men stood before the people.
One was Jesus Christ — the healer, the teacher, the man who opened blind eyes and raised the dead.
The other was Barabbas — a rebel, a violent criminal, a man whose hands knew blood.
And the governor Pontius Pilate asked the question that split history in two:

“Which one do you want me to release to you?”
— Matthew 27:21
The crowd answered.
“Barabbas.”
Think about that moment.
A murderer stood beside the Son of God.
And the people chose…
the murderer.

Not the healer.
Not the innocent man.
The criminal.
But here is the thunder of the Gospel.
The guilty walked free.

Barabbas deserved the cross.
Rome built crosses for men like him.
But that day…
Jesus took it instead.

The innocent condemned.
The guilty released.
That is not just Barabbas’ story.
That is ours.

Every lie.
Every hidden sin.
Every moment we chose darkness over light.
We stand where Barabbas stood.
Guilty.
Yet the Gospel whispers something scandalous:
Christ takes our cross.

“But he was pierced for our transgressions…
the punishment that brought us peace was on him.”
— Isaiah 53:5

The cross meant for the rebel
became the throne of grace.
Imagine Barabbas walking out of that prison.

Chains removed.
Legs shaking.
Sunlight hitting his face.
Behind him…
Jesus walking toward Golgotha.
For him.
For us.
The crowd chose a criminal.
But heaven chose a Savior.
And today the question turns toward you.
What will you do with Jesus?

Repent.
Turn to Christ.
Receive the freedom He purchased with His blood.
Because the truth still stands:

The guilty walked free…
because Jesus took their place.
